newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Zairean peace talks resume in South Africa.
newsitem.headline: Zairean peace talks resume in South Africa.

text.p: Zairean peace talks resumed in South Africa on Monday as news broke of a rebel advance to within 30 km (20 miles) of the key mining centre and second largest city of Lubumbashi, a spokesman said.

South African foreign ministry spokesman Peter Swanepoel said full delegations representing the government of President Mobutu Sese Seko and rebel leader Laurent Kabila resumed talks shortly after 10 a.m. (0800 GMT) at an undisclosed venue near Pretoria.
"The full delegations last met from 10 p.m. on Sunday until after midnight and they are just sitting down now to start again," he told Reuters.
The talks resumed shortly after residents of Kipushi told Reuters by telephone that the town had fallen to rebels who continued walking towards Lubumbashi, about 30 km (20 miles) down the road.
